question: Can small expert symmetry-breaking noise overcome cloned-expert degeneracy and create useful conditional specialization without destroying the Cell-DINO starting representation?
hypothesis: A 0.001 or 0.01 relative perturbation of cloned expert input weights will increase randomized-router reliance and reduce dead-expert behavior relative to the active zero-noise temperature-0.3 anchors, while retaining ID and improving mean or worst-experiment OOD validation.
predicted_signature: Noise 0.001 at E8, or noise 0.01 at one adjacent bank, produces route reliance above 0.01 by epoch 30 with an OOD-validation or worst-experiment improvement and no more than two ID points lost versus the exact shared zero-noise anchor.
alternative_explanation: Any gain is ordinary weight-noise regularization rather than conditional specialization; pressure-matched zero-noise anchors and route-reliance diagnostics separate these explanations.
falsifier: All noisy arms retain route reliance at or below 0.01, lose ID, or fail to improve mean or worst-experiment OOD validation versus their pressure-, bank-, objective-, seed-, and schedule-matched zero-noise anchors.
pruning_rule: At epoch 10 prune a noisy arm dominated by its shared zero-noise anchor on OOD validation, ID retention, worst-experiment accuracy, and route reliance unless differentiation is increasing. Continue to epoch 60 only for a competitive epoch-30 trajectory or route reliance above 0.01.
checkpoint_policy: save epochs 10, 30, and 60 for every arm reaching the milestone
multiplicity: Exploratory eight-arm symmetry-breaking screen opened after broad router, pressure, expert-count, temperature, and auxiliary searches; no winner is confirmatory without locked fresh seeds and a matched dense noise control.
